mappings.rationale: Step consists entirely of cf_export calls and shell variable assignments with no identifiable command pattern in the mapping table. A run: step is emitted that rewrites cf_export calls to $GITHUB_OUTPUT / $GITHUB_ENV equivalents, but the exact variable names and downstream consumers must be verified manually.

Step uses assume-role-with-web-identity via the AWS CLI with a mounted OIDC token file — a Codefresh-specific mechanism. GitHub Actions provides native OIDC support through the id-token permission and aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4. The translation is non-trivial: the IAM role trust policy must be updated to trust the GHA OIDC provider, and all downstream cf_export'd credentials must be removed in favour of the action's implicit environment injection.

Codefresh git-clone step maps deterministically to actions/checkout@v4. The repo and revision fields translate directly to the repository and ref inputs. fetch-depth: 0 is added to preserve full history, matching CF default behaviour.

CF step.build maps deterministically to docker/build-push-action@v5 with push: false. The build_arguments array translates to the build-args multi-line input. GHA layer caching via type=gha is added as a performance improvement over CF's default no-cache behaviour.

CF step.push maps to docker/build-push-action@v5 with push: true. The tags array (IMAGE_TAG and latest) translates directly to the tags multi-line input. The registry field refers to the ECR integration configured in Codefresh; in GHA this is replaced by aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login@v2 in a preceding step.

Freestyle step running npm ci + npm test matches the freestyle-to-run pattern. Confidence is medium rather than high because the working_directory was set to the git_clone step output (${{git_clone}}), which relies on CF volume sharing between steps — in GHA each job gets a fresh checkout, so the checkout must be repeated. The commands themselves transfer cleanly.

The sonar-scanner CLI image (sonarsource/sonar-scanner-cli:5) has no direct GHA action mapping in the current KB. SonarSource publishes an official action (SonarSource/sonarqube-scan-action@v3 or SonarSource/sonarcloud-github-action) that is strongly preferred over running the CLI directly. The qualitygate.wait=true flag also needs translation: the official action handles quality gate polling natively. Manual configuration of the SonarQube project and SONAR_TOKEN secret is required.

The command (npm run test:integration) maps cleanly via the freestyle-to-run pattern, but the CF retry block (maxAttempts: 3, delay: 30s) has no native GHA equivalent at the step level. Retry logic in GHA requires either the nick-fields/retry-action wrapper, a shell loop, or promotion to a job-level strategy.fail-fast configuration. The retry semantics are omitted in the generated step and flagged for manual addition.

CF step.deploy with kind: helm maps to a helm upgrade --install run step under a GHA environment gate (environment: staging). The kube_context, namespace, chart_name, release_name, and set values all transfer directly. Confidence is medium because the Helm release name (crm-staging) differs from the CF release_name field by convention — verify this is intentional. The GHA job uses environment: staging to enforce branch protection and required reviewers.

The CF step runs Newman (Postman CLI) via the postman/newman:6-alpine image. There is no official Newman GitHub Action in the current KB. The mapping falls back to a raw run: step using npx newman, which changes the execution environment from the CF Docker container to the runner's Node.js. The --env-var flags translate directly, but the API_KEY value must be moved from a CF context variable (${{STAGING_API_KEY}}) to a GitHub secret (${{ secrets.STAGING_API_KEY }}).

Production Helm deployment requires manual review for three reasons: (1) the CF pipeline has no rollback or blue/green strategy — this is a risk in production GHA workflows and should be addressed before migration; (2) the when.branch.only: [main] guard in CF does not automatically translate to if: github.ref conditions without verifying that branch protection rules are correctly enforced; (3) production deployments should use --atomic --timeout flags and a dedicated Helm diff preview step. A placeholder run: step is emitted with detailed TODO comments.

Curl-based webhook notification maps via the freestyle-to-run pattern. Confidence is low because the CF when condition (deploy_to_production.result == success) uses CF expression syntax that does not transfer — in GHA this becomes if: needs.production.result == 'success', but the notify job already uses if: always() to ensure it runs regardless. The CF_BUILD_INITIATOR variable maps to github.actor. The TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL must be stored as a GitHub secret rather than a CF context variable.
